$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
3k=-6\,⟹\,k=-2.
$$

But then

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}\ne \begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$
